checks_run.procedure: Judge D-229 (connector configuration names stay cannot-name) and the D-228 (4) ruling that cross-organization ids are out of scope. Look for a served column, response, notification channel or write path that still names a sensitive record, or a token sequence that loses or misplaces a hidden literal. New this round: a probe of the automation dry-run's conditionsMet as a channel, and a source read of the action parameter schemas.
checks_run.command: repro/zz-sec-r7-dryrun-condition-oracle.test.ts (copied to apps/api/test/integration/access/ and removed); source read of versions.ts:348-523, dry-run.ts:120-230 and packages/shared/src/schemas/automation.ts:95-200
checks_run.environment: $TMPDIR/rv at d8868b2a5; Node v22.22.0; disposable PostgreSQL on port 32465.
checks_run.expected: No served path names a hidden record; any residual is within an accepted ruling.
checks_run.actual:
No defect, so no finding.
(a) Token sequences: SEC-R7-23 passes. Positions count every literal of the stored version. The tag is an HMAC over (row key, id, row version) and is resolved under If-Match, so edits, grant changes and concurrent saves cannot misplace a literal.
(b) Action parameters cannot carry a sensitive record id. create_task, notify and escalate are strict schemas (role, message key, optional targetTransformationId); starter parameters are integers. The summary shows only the role.
(c) Dry runs store and serve plannedActions and findings {code, pointer, field}, never a condition value. The probe's version read and dry-run list name the hidden id X nowhere.
(d) The probe (40, 1/1, exit 0) confirms a 1-bit oracle. An ADM_METHOD author shown '[restricted:<tag>:1]' gets conditionsMet true for a sample with benefitId = X, and false for a visible id or a random uuid. To use it, the author must already hold X; UUIDv7 ids are not guessable, and the reply discloses no content.
This is the residual ADR-0051 already accepts at line 353 (BE-Z12 §3, D-223 (2)): 'A writer who already holds a hidden id learns that it names a restricted record.' My old-branch predecessor recorded the same 'o1' observation (39-token-probes.log). I judge it an observation.
(e) D-229: connector field-mapping sources and SecretRef names are text that administrators or IT write and already see, not a reference the product creates. I accept cannot-name.
(f) D-228 (4): markedInOrganizations covers every organization of the principal, so another organization's id resolves to nothing the caller could not already reach. I accept the out-of-scope ruling.
The product tree is unchanged since my round-3/5 judgement.
